nodes.summary: Two single-linkage clusters of the same subset that share a point are equal, since clusters are equivalence classes; so the clusters of `A` partition `A` (Carlsson, *Topology and data*, Bull. AMS 2009, §3.2: single linkage produces a partition of the point cloud).
nodes.title: Clusters of a subset are disjoint or equal

nodes.summary: Every point of `A` lies in a single-linkage cluster of `A`, so the clusters of the preimages `f⁻¹(U α)` cover `X` when the `U α` cover the image of `f` (Carlsson, *Topology and data*, Bull. AMS 2009, §3.2, step (4): the clusters form a covering of `X`).
nodes.title: The clusters of a subset cover it

nodes.summary: If the covering has dimension at most `n`, i.e. any finite set of indices whose sets `U i` have a common point has at most `n + 1` elements, then every simplex of the Mapper complex has at most `n + 1` vertices (Carlsson, *Topology and data*, Bull. AMS 2009, §3.2, the remark after step (5)). Clusters of the same preimage that share a point coincide, so the vertices of a simplex lie over distinct cover elements.
nodes.title: Dimension of the Mapper complex

nodes.summary: For a dissimilarity `d` on `X`, a scale `ε`, a filter `f : X → Z` and a family `U : ι → Set Z` (a covering of the reference space), the Mapper complex is the nerve of the family of single-linkage clusters `c` of the preimages `f⁻¹(U α)`, indexed by the pairs `(α, c)`: a finite set of such pairs spans a simplex when the clusters have a point in common (Carlsson, *Topology and data*, Bull. AMS 2009, §3.2, steps…
nodes.title: Mapper complex

nodes.summary: The clusters at scale `ε` of a subset `A ⊆ X` are the classes of `ε`-equivalence for the dissimilarity `d` restricted to `A`, viewed as subsets of `X`: chains must stay inside `A` (Carlsson, *Topology and data*, Bull. AMS 2009, §3.2, step (4)).
nodes.title: Single-linkage clusters of a subset

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
